chunks: And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from his brother Ali, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sabah, who said: Anas narrated to me from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
He said: Every proud and stubborn person is one who refuses to say 'La ilaha illallah' (There is no god but Allah).

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: The declaration of monotheism (La ilaha illallah)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be a 'jabbar' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq links the spiritual state of arrogance to the verbal affirmation of *Tawhid*, suggesting that the refusal to declare 'La ilaha illallah' is the root of the 'jabbar's' stubbornness. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the interplay between inner conviction and outward declaration, where the heart's resistance manifests as a rejection of the core creed. The hadith thus elevates the recitation of the declaration from a mere ritual to a definitive test of humility and submission to God.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3. And from the previous chain from al-Hussain b. Sayf from his brother Ali from his father from al-Hassan b. al-Sabah who said it was narrated to me by Anas from The Prophet (s.a.w.s.)
who said: “One who does not recite Laa ilaaha illallaah is proud and arrogant.”
